editorial.headline: Flower Wholesale: Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale flower and ornamental-plant activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but foreign investors cannot register it in Bali under the permanent provincial moratorium.
editorial.body:
**In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this wholesale activity today.** Nationally, it is open to PMA with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali’s record, however, marks it blocked for PMA: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it within the Bali moratorium recorded in May 2026. The national opening is real; on the island, however, it does not enable PMA registration.

The activity concerns wholesale trade in agricultural outputs from flowers and other ornamental plants. Its stated examples include roses, jasmine, ornamental-plant seedlings, and flower seedlings. The commercial subject is therefore the wholesale movement of flowering and ornamental plant material, including nursery stock identified in the scope. It is a category defined by the products being traded: flowers and ornamental plants, rather than a single named crop or a narrower product line.

National registration is open across the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the activity is not confined to one business size in the national record. Yet it does not alter the Bali result for PMA. The provincial block is stated directly, and the record identifies the relevant risk position at the Besar scale as Low or Medium-Low across every scope. For a founder assessing foreign participation, the distinction is straightforward: the national ownership ceiling establishes what is open nationally, while Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule determines whether PMA registration can proceed there.

This is not a marginal caveat to be handled after the business model is settled. It is the central jurisdictional fact for a foreign-owned wholesale operation involving flowers and ornamental plants in Bali. The national PMA position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021; the Bali position is tied to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. Read together, those entries support a precise conclusion: full foreign ownership is available nationally, but Bali blocks PMA registration for this activity under its stated moratorium.
